claims.title: Papuan settlers reach the islands
claims.summary: Papuan-speaking peoples occupy the main Solomon chain, part of Near Oceania, in some of the earliest recorded sea crossings by humans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-30000bce-papuan-settlers-reach-the-islands, claim TL:SLB:event:30000bce:papuan-settlers-reach-the-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arrival of the Lapita
claims.summary: Austronesian-speaking Lapita voyagers, ancestors of much of the later Pacific, settle the islands and mix with existing populations.

sources.label: Lapita Culture and the Arrival of Asians in the Pacific

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1000bce-arrival-of-the-lapita, claim TL:SLB:event:1000bce:arrival-of-the-lapita, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mendaña reaches and names the islands
claims.summary: Álvaro de Mendaña becomes the first European to reach the archipelago; rumoured gold leads to the name 'Solomon Islands' after the biblical king.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1568-mendana-reaches-and-names-the-islands, claim TL:SLB:event:1568:mendana-reaches-and-names-the-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mendaña's failed colony
claims.summary: A second Spanish expedition attempts a settlement in the Santa Cruz islands but collapses amid disease and conflict; Mendaña dies there.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1595-mendana-s-failed-colony, claim TL:SLB:event:1595:mendana-s-failed-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The blackbirding labour trade
claims.summary: Recruiters carry tens of thousands of Solomon Islanders, many coerced, to plantations in Queensland and Fiji, bringing disease and depopulation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1863-the-blackbirding-labour-trade, claim TL:SLB:event:1863:the-blackbirding-labour-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Killing of Bishop Patteson
claims.summary: John Coleridge Patteson, first Anglican Bishop of Melanesia, is killed at Nukapu, reportedly in reprisal for blackbirders' raids on islanders.

sources.label: John Coleridge Patteson, Missionary Bishop of Melanesia

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1871-killing-of-bishop-patteson, claim TL:SLB:event:1871:killing-of-bishop-patteson, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British protectorate proclaimed
claims.summary: Britain declares a protectorate over the southern Solomons to curb labour-trade abuses and forestall French and German expansion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1893-british-protectorate-proclaimed, claim TL:SLB:event:1893:british-protectorate-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Germany cedes the northern islands
claims.summary: Germany transfers most of the northern Solomons to Britain in exchange for recognition of its claims elsewhere, enlarging the protectorate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1899-germany-cedes-the-northern-islands, claim TL:SLB:event:1899:germany-cedes-the-northern-islands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: US landings on Guadalcanal
claims.summary: US Marines land on Guadalcanal and Tulagi in the first major American amphibious offensive of the war, seizing the future Henderson Field.

sources.label: The Battle of Guadalcanal
sources.publisher: The National WWII Museum, New Orleans

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1942-us-landings-on-guadalcanal, claim TL:SLB:event:1942:us-landings-on-guadalcanal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese evacuate Guadalcanal
claims.summary: After a six-month seesaw campaign, Japan withdraws its forces; Guadalcanal becomes a turning point of the Pacific War.

sources.label: The Battle of Guadalcanal
sources.publisher: The National WWII Museum, New Orleans

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1943-japanese-evacuate-guadalcanal, claim TL:SLB:event:1943:japanese-evacuate-guadalcanal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Maasina Rule movement
claims.summary: A post-war Malaitan movement for self-government and custom, born of the wartime labour corps, is credited as an early step toward independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1944-the-maasina-rule-movement, claim TL:SLB:event:1944:the-maasina-rule-movement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Internal self-government
claims.summary: Solomon Islands attains internal self-government, the final constitutional step before independence, with Peter Kenilorea as chief minister.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1976-internal-self-government, claim TL:SLB:event:1976:internal-self-government, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from the United Kingdom
claims.summary: The protectorate becomes the independent state of Solomon Islands within the Commonwealth, with Sir Peter Kenilorea as first prime minister.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With the Solomon Islands

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1978-independence-from-the-united-kingdom, claim TL:SLB:event:1978:independence-from-the-united-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The United States recognises the new state
claims.summary: Senator John Glenn delivers President Carter's letter of recognition to Prime Minister Kenilorea on independence day itself; diplomatic relations follow on 9 October.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Solomon Islands
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1978-the-united-states-recognises-the-new-state, claim TL:SLB:event:1978:the-united-states-recognises-the-new-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Melanesian Spearhead Group
claims.summary: Solomon Islands joins Vanuatu and Papua New Guinea in a bloc formed to preserve Melanesian cultural traditions — small Pacific states organising around what they share.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1988-the-melanesian-spearhead-group, claim TL:SLB:event:1988:the-melanesian-spearhead-group, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Tensions
claims.summary: Ethnic conflict between Guadalcanal and Malaitan groups around Honiara displaces thousands and, in 2000, topples Prime Minister Ulufa'alu.

sources.label: Australian peacekeepers in Solomon Islands, 2000–2017
sources.publisher: Australian Government (Anzac Portal, Dept of Veterans' Affairs)

claims.title: East Rennell inscribed, and later imperilled
claims.summary: The southern third of Rennell Island — the largest raised coral atoll in the world — joins the World Heritage List; it is moved to the List in Danger in 2013.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-1998-east-rennell-inscribed-and-later-imperilled, claim TL:SLB:event:1998:east-rennell-inscribed-and-later-imperilled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Malaita Eagle Force coup
claims.summary: Militants take Prime Minister Ulufa'alu hostage and force his resignation; an Australian-brokered treaty that October begins a weapons handover that does not hold.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-2000-the-malaita-eagle-force-coup, claim TL:SLB:event:2000:the-malaita-eagle-force-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cyclone Zoe strikes Tikopia
claims.summary: A cyclone devastates the remote islands of Tikopia and Anuta; a relief vessel sails expecting mass casualties and finds nobody killed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Solomon Islands: An archipelago misnamed for a king's gold, forged by settlement, war and sovereignty", terralore.co/country/SLB/chronicle#ev-2002-cyclone-zoe-strikes-tikopia, claim TL:SLB:event:2002:cyclone-zoe-strikes-tikopia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: RAMSI intervention
claims.summary: At the government's request, Australia leads a multinational mission that restores order, disarms militias and rebuilds institutions until 2017.

sources.publisher: Australian Government (Anzac Portal, Dept of Veterans' Affairs)

claims.title: Harold Keke surrenders
claims.summary: The Isatabu Freedom Movement leader gives himself up to Australian forces and is charged with the murder of the priest and MP Augustine Geve.
